lead: A Rust test can be leaning on a request having *no* handler, and its title says nothing about which one.
body: `nvs-lsp`'s `a_tree_of_cases_reports_one_summary_line` builds a two-case tree it expects to score `0 passed, 2 failed`, and one of those cases failed only because `answer` had no `completion` arm — so landing the arm turned a fixture into a pass and broke a test about summary lines. Before implementing a `.lspt` request, grep the crate's own tests for its name and re-point any fixture that was failing for want of a handler at a genuinely mismatched `--EXPECT--`.
